messages:
matt: FYI — after we flipped on strict fncall schema validation last night, the console shows a huge spike in schema_rejects for the tool-invoke route and quotas are getting weirdly attributed to the fallback route. billing numbers don't line up with reject counts. anyone seen this?

olivia: saw the alert this morning. looks like rejects > 60% for a subset of customers. does the telemetry include validate_reason currently?

raj: not reliably — the new validator tag (schema_v2) was added but sampling was changed at rollout. I suspect the sampling key used by the metrics pipeline omitted the route_id when validate_reason was set, so counters got folded into default route.

matt: do we have a query to prove that? I pulled the console graph and it shows fallback_route spike exactly when validator rollout finished.

raj: here's the quick ES query I ran (pseudo):
```
GET /metrics/_search
{ "query": { "bool": { "must": [{ "term": { "event": "schema_reject" }}, { "range": { "@timestamp": { "gte": "now-24h" }}}]}}
```
group by: route_id, validate_mode (strict|permissive|soft)

raj: results had many hits with route_id=null and validate_mode=strict — sampling layer dropped route tag on strict path.

devex-anna: this matches a customer ticket — they saw their usage spike under "fallback" and got quota warnings. we should patch sampling asap and add a retro tag for misattributed windows to reconcile billing.

olivia: agree. short-term mitigation: can we flip strict->soft for the canary slice while fixing sampler? that will stop rejects and revert behavior for impacted customers.

matt: can do a targeted toggle. admin api payload to change validation mode for a rollout slice: 
```
PATCH /api/v1/rollouts/validators/1234
{
  "slice": "canary-5pct",
  "validation_mode": "soft"
}
```
I'll run it after approval.

deploy-bot: rollout 1234: validator-mode -> strict completed at 2025-11-07T03:12:11Z (canary-5pct).

console-bot: alert: schema_reject_rate > 50% for route tool-invoke (eu-west-1) — triggered 1744299000 (investigate).

raj: I pushed a quick fix idea to the telemetry repo: ensure the sampling stage preserves route_id and attach validate_reason label. patch: add route_id to sampled_keys and emit validate_reason as label. will open PR.

devex-anna: for customer communication: propose we (1) temporarily soft-fail canary, (2) mark the misattributed window, (3) run a reconciliation job to reassign counts. I'll draft a short note.

olivia: timeline? we should avoid a full rollback. patch + toggle sounds fine. how long to get PR reviewed and hotfixed?

raj: I can get a small PR up in 20m, request urgent review. if approved, staging -> hotfix -> prod in ~90m.

matt: I'll request approval from infra on the toggle and then execute. can someone add a dashboard card showing validate_reason and route_id together (even if sparse) so we can watch the fix live?

devex-anna: adding card now, will ping here when done. also adding a column to the billing reconciliation export for validate_reason.

olivia: thanks. once patch is in, we should run a low-cost backfill to re-tag events in the 2h window and produce a reconciliation delta for billing ops.

matt: sounds good. action items: raj -> PR+hotfix; devex-anna -> customer comms + reconciliation column; me -> toggle canary after approval; olivia -> coordinate billing ops.

raj: PR opened: github.com/redwood/telemetry/pull/742 (label: hotfix). requesting @olivia for urgent review.

deploy-bot: rollback option available for rollout 1234 (canary-5pct). use `/deploy rollback 1234` to revert.

devex-anna: draft note to affected customers uploaded to docs/running/incident-notes.md — sharing soon.

matt: ok i'll hold for olivia review then flip to soft for canary. once patch is in we watch the validate_reason column. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
